story.title: Ferry Capsizes off Northern Cyprus, Leaving Several Dead and Many Missing
story.summary: A ferry carrying nearly 270 passengers and crew capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus, resulting in at least seven confirmed deaths. Local authorities reported that 237 individuals have been rescued, while 23 remain unaccounted for. Rescue operations are ongoing as search teams work to locate those missing.

explore_lenses.label: Why do the casualty figures differ?
explore_lenses.title: The toll is changing as rescuers account for people
explore_lenses.summary: The initial counts were operational snapshots rather than a final manifest reconciliation. Later local reporting cited the transport minister saying the death toll had risen while the number still being sought had fallen.

claims.text: Turkey's Interior Ministry said FILOJET left Girne for Taşucu with 259 passengers and eight crew members, for a total of 267 people.
Transport Minister Erhan Arıklı later said eight people had died and 17 were still being sought; that differs from earlier reports of seven deaths and 23 missing.
The differing totals indicate that authorities were still reconciling rescues, fatalities and the passenger list, rather than issuing a settled final count.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about why the ferry sank?
explore_lenses.title: Water ingress is confirmed; the cause is not
explore_lenses.summary: Officials agree the catamaran began taking on water soon after departure, but they had not established why. Rough conditions were reported, yet officials cautioned against treating weather as a proven cause.

claims.text: The vessel began taking on water roughly 15 minutes after departure, about 7.5 kilometres (four nautical miles) offshore, before it capsized.
Prime Minister Ünal Üstel described adverse weather and waves before the vessel took on water, according to reports citing him.
Transport Minister Erhan Arıklı said there was not yet a finding on the cause of the water ingress; he later said investigators would need to reach the vessel's recorder to determine why it sank.
Filo Denizcilik said it had opened a crisis desk and was coordinating with authorized rescue teams, but its statement did not offer an explanation for the accident.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the rescue and inquiry?
explore_lenses.title: Deep-water recovery and a criminal inquiry are under way
explore_lenses.summary: The next phase combines continuing searches with an investigation into possible negligence. The reported depth of the wreck makes underwater work central to both efforts.

claims.text: Turkish and northern Cypriot authorities deployed coast-guard vessels, helicopters, naval units and a civilian passenger vessel to the search area.
Prime Minister Üstel said the captain and seven staff members had been detained as an investigation began, while stressing that any negligence would be examined.
Forecast: Üstel said a naval search-and-rescue vessel capable of operating to 1,000 metres would arrive shortly to help search the wreck and missing people.
Officials said the ferry had sunk in water about 514 metres deep, a condition that complicates access to the vessel and potential recovery of evidence.

story_report.summary: A ferry travelling from Girne in northern Cyprus to Taşucu, Turkey, capsized shortly after leaving port, triggering a large search-and-rescue operation. The FILOJET was carrying 267 people, including 259 passengers and eight crew members. Initial official figures recorded seven deaths, 237 rescues and 23 people unaccounted for; later figures reported eight deaths and 17 still being sought, indicating that authorities were continuing to reconcile the toll.

sections.heading: Ferry Took Water Offshore
sections.body: The vessel began taking on water about 15 minutes after departure, roughly 7.5 kilometres, or four nautical miles, offshore, before capsizing. Prime Minister Ünal Üstel said adverse weather and waves preceded the flooding. However, Transport Minister Erhan Arıklı said no finding had yet established why water entered the ferry, and said investigators would need access to the vessel’s recorder to determine the cause of the sinking.

sections.heading: Deep-Water Search and Investigation
sections.body: Turkish and northern Cypriot authorities sent coast-guard vessels, helicopters, naval units and a civilian passenger vessel to search for survivors and the missing. Officials said the ferry sank in water about 514 metres deep, complicating access to the wreck and possible recovery of evidence. Üstel said the captain and seven other staff members had been detained as an investigation began, while a naval search-and-rescue vessel capable of operating to 1,000 metres was expected to assist.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not issued a final, independently confirmed accounting of all people aboard; reported death and missing-person figures differed as rescue and passenger-list information was reconciled.

No official finding had identified the cause of the water ingress or sinking. The detentions of the captain and seven staff members do not establish criminal responsibility, and no investigation outcome or timetable was available.

related_stories.title: Death Toll from Nepal-Tibet Floods Approaches 800 with Thousands Missing
related_stories.summary: Rescue efforts continue in the aftermath of catastrophic flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region, with the death toll reaching nearly 800. As of now, over 3,000 people remain unaccounted for, including 2,502 in Nepal and 546 in Tibet. Heavy rain is hampering rescue operations, complicating the search for survivors.

related_stories.title: Nepal Issues Flood Warning as Communities Face Ongoing Challenges
related_stories.summary: Authorities in Nepal have issued warnings of potential fresh flooding, urging residents in affected districts to stay alert. This comes as water levels in the Bhotekoshi River have risen, exacerbating the challenges faced by communities already grappling with the aftermath of previous flooding events.
